| [NOTE-029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md) | Krauska & Lau 2023, moving away from lexicalism | Standard production and comprehension models built on "lemmas" (stored triads of meaning, syntax and form, with syntax stopping at the word) inherit a lexicalist assumption that typology has refuted. Replacing that assumption needs new algorithms, not just new representations: separate meaning↔syntax and syntax↔form mappings with one integrated stage for retrieving and assembling syntactic structure. This predicts different aphasia profiles. | Skimmed |

| [NOTE-052](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-052.md) | Consciousness in AI: indicator properties | Assuming computational functionalism, the report derives a rubric of 14 "indicator properties" from leading neuroscientific theories of consciousness (RPT, GWT, computational HOTs, AST, PP, agency and embodiment). | [NOTE-055](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-055.md) | Pilgrim et al. 2025, foundations of collective intelligence | The known forms of collective intelligence (wisdom of crowds, collective sensing, division of labour, cultural learning) can all be derived from one principle.
